title: Comparative outcomes require common denominators
summary: A comparison and inference protocol: 24 entity coverage states now carry exact continuation decisions through Phase 56R, while parent action, child recommendation, artifact state, milestone, official review, closure, operating outcome, period, denominator, and reopening boundaries remain attached.
map_question: When can operating records support a comparison, and when must they remain parallel evidence trails?
interpretation_boundary: The map governs within-domain longitudinal claims. It is not a score, ranking, forecast, or claim that different operating systems share one outcome direction.

nodes.label: AI and cyber outcomes
nodes.note: Inventory, maturity, implementation, incident, and benefit measures remain distinct.

nodes.label: Manufacturing outcomes
nodes.note: Participation, completion, placement, sales, savings, jobs, quality, and productivity use different denominators.

nodes.label: Infrastructure outcomes
nodes.note: Capacity, service, reliability, commodity, and water measures answer different questions.

nodes.label: Mobility and mission outcomes
nodes.note: Trips, flights, miles, incidents, operations, missions, and cargo must retain system context.

nodes.label: Unit and denominator
nodes.note: The quantity and population or exposure base must match.

nodes.label: Period, geography, and method
nodes.note: Records must cover compatible time, place, scope, and collection rules.

nodes.label: Attribution and validation
nodes.note: Official, audited, company-attributed, and modeled results must remain labeled.

nodes.label: Comparable outcome evidence
nodes.note: Comparison begins only after the measurement contracts align.

nodes.label: Compatible time points
nodes.note: At least two observations must share the measurement contract before direction is described.

nodes.label: Revisions and series breaks
nodes.note: Vintages, method changes, combined years, and discontinued definitions remain first-class evidence.

nodes.label: Bounded longitudinal read
nodes.note: Direction is published inside one defined series without becoming a composite score.

nodes.label: Stable entity identity
nodes.note: Agency, facility, plant code, or operating-carrier identity must persist across observations.

nodes.label: Bounded entity operating panel
nodes.note: At least two compatible observations can publish inside one named entity without becoming a rank.

nodes.label: Entity driver and constraint dossier
nodes.note: Baseline, intervention or input, constraint, and later observation are ordered inside one stable entity.

nodes.label: Causal-inference hold
nodes.note: Attribution and temporal sequence do not establish an independently validated causal effect.

nodes.label: Repeat outcome or alternative-explanation test
nodes.note: A later record maps to named alternatives and declares compatibility, attribution, and validation status.

nodes.label: Denominator or method break
nodes.note: Different units, methods, identities, windows, and attribution levels stop silent series extension.

nodes.label: Four-record entity sufficiency screen
nodes.note: A candidate enters only when stable identity and at least four primary or official records support all three layers.

nodes.label: Second-cohort panel, dossier, and test
nodes.note: All twelve retained entities carry the same three-layer publication contract.

nodes.label: 24-entity one-record coverage ledger
nodes.note: One record is Closed, sixteen are Partially Closed, and seven remain Open under named reopening rules.

nodes.label: Seven exact-record acquisition checks
nodes.note: Dalrymple advances to Partially Closed; six selected records remain Open under dated continuation rules.

nodes.label: Fourteen acquisition and deepening decisions
nodes.note: DOE, F-35, and Hornsdale advance to Partially Closed; three exact rails remain Open and eight partial records deepen.

nodes.label: Twelve remaining first-pass decisions
nodes.note: Three Open and nine Partially Closed records retain their states; two genuinely new bounded denominators publish.

nodes.label: Ordered continuation queue and five named decisions
nodes.note: Manatee moves to Partially Closed; four other records preserve bounded findings or holds.

nodes.label: Seven exact-record decisions
nodes.note: Three bounded observations publish; four verified non-closures remain explicit; no evidence state changes.

nodes.label: Three manufacturer realized-outcome decisions
nodes.note: Two certified reported-employment records publish; one repeat-series non-closure remains explicit; no evidence state changes.

nodes.label: Three federal remediation and component outcome records
nodes.note: One NASA exact non-closure and two HHS provider control tests publish; no evidence state changes.

nodes.label: Ten verified remediation and component decisions
nodes.note: Nine bounded records publish and one dated HHS tracker check remains held; no Phase 56F evidence state changes.

nodes.label: Eight cross-agency remediation follow-through records
nodes.note: Seven agency portfolios and one government-wide model publish; no Phase 56F evidence state changes.

nodes.label: Twenty-two letter-named priority actions
nodes.note: Five DOE, four HHS, eight DOT, and five VA actions publish under local keys; no Phase 56F evidence state changes.

nodes.label: Twenty exact identities and two held mappings
nodes.note: Twenty Phase 56P actions resolve one-to-one; HHS-04 and VA-02 remain held as one-to-many mappings.

nodes.label: Twenty-four recommendation artifact and milestone records
nodes.note: Twenty exact continuations plus four recommendation-specific children preserve the implementation-state boundary.

links.note: Use-case counts do not share a denominator with mission or productivity outcomes.
Engagements, graduates, jobs, dollars, and quality measures are not interchangeable.
Grid, water, storage, and mineral results differ by asset, customer, commodity, region, and period.
Road, airline, and space operating systems use different reporting regimes.
Compatible denominators are incomplete in several portfolios.
Periods, geographies, and methods are not consistently aligned.
Attributed results require validation before causal interpretation.
Compatible observations permit a bounded direction statement.
A material series break stops or restates the line.
Longitudinal evidence remains within-domain and does not close cross-system comparability.
A stable entity ID prevents name changes, mergers, exits, and denominator drift from silently rewriting the line.
Entity panels remain bounded and do not close cross-entity comparability.
Every dossier inherits the parent panel's stable entity and measurement contract.
Alternative explanations and validation limits remain attached to every association.
Repeated compatible outcomes and independent validation are incomplete.
Every test inherits the Phase 56C entity, dossier, and named alternatives.
Compatibility is declared before interpreting the later record.
A broken or missing denominator prevents causal or performance interpretation.
Twelve of twelve candidates passed the four-record screen.
The vertical contract preserves method, attribution, identity, and denominator breaks.
Four portfolio interpretations remain held even though all 36 entity layers publish.
A coverage decision cannot bridge an incompatible unit, denominator, period, method, identity, or attribution break.
The cross-cohort interpretation remains In Review; closure states are evidence states, not performance or causal measures.
Every acquisition retains its Phase 56F coverage ID and reopening rule.
Six checked sources remain incompatible with the selected annual, monthly, interval, investigation, or restoration record.
Acquisition and closure states do not measure performance and support no causal inference or ranking.
All six Phase 56G Open rails receive another named-source check and three advance on compatible records.
Annual summaries, cumulative totals, recommendation status, and event counts remain bounded by missing monthly, interval, closure, restoration, or outcome denominators.
Acquisition and evidence-state movement do not measure performance and support no causal inference, ranking, or score.
Phase 56I continues the three remaining Open rails and completes the nine-record partial first pass.
Monthly releases, program commitments, project descriptions, and current source checks retain annual, interval, execution, restoration, and outcome gaps.
First-pass completion and evidence availability do not measure performance and support no causal inference, ranking, or score.
Phase 56J begins from the completed 24-entity first-pass ledger and preserves every stable ID and continuation rule.
Monthly, constraint, event, plan, and component scopes remain incompatible with complete interval, annual, fleet, or department-wide outcomes.
Evidence priority and disclosure do not measure entity performance and support no ranking, score, or causal inference.
Phase 56K executes the next seven named continuation rules without replacing stable IDs or evidence states.
Each current observation remains bounded to its actual entity, period, source role, and denominator.
Publication, non-publication, recommendation status, and delivery timing do not establish comparative performance or causation.
Phase 56L executes the next three named manufacturer continuation rules without replacing stable IDs or evidence states.
Employment, project amount, completion, and operating output retain their actual entity, project, period, and source role.
Reported current employment and project completion do not establish project causation or comparative performance.
Phase 56M executes two named federal continuation rules with exact recommendation and component-test records.
Agency recommendations and anonymous provider tests retain different identities, scopes, periods, frameworks, and denominators.
No record establishes department-wide effectiveness, sector performance, real-incident outcomes, or patient causation.
Phase 56N continues the federal recommendation rail with exact action, portfolio, and component states.
Plans, inventories, portfolios, programs, and facility inspections retain different identities, scopes, periods, and denominators.
No recommendation or component status establishes system performance, enterprise effectiveness, service outcomes, or causation.
Phase 56O continues the exact remediation rail from action and component status into annual agency portfolio movement.
Agency inventories, subject mixes, additions, removals, implementation counts, and model assumptions are not shared denominators.
Portfolio movement and modeled potential benefits do not establish performance, realized savings, service outcomes, or causation.
Phase 56P decomposes four Phase 56O portfolios into action text explicitly named by the official letters.
Local action keys, underlying recommendation identities, agency responses, and implementation states are not interchangeable denominators.
A named open priority action does not establish performance, operating outcomes, savings, readiness, safety, or causation.
Phase 56Q resolves the local action identities established in Phase 56P.
Local actions, official recommendations, response states, closure states, and operating outcomes are distinct denominators.
Identity and response evidence do not establish performance, value, readiness, safety, or causation.
Phase 56R follows the official identities and two held parents established in Phase 56Q.
Parent action, child recommendation, artifact, milestone, review, closure, and outcome use different denominators.
Artifacts and milestones do not establish performance, value, readiness, safety, savings, or causation.

what_this_map_supports: FTFN can publish bounded outcome records while preserving their original measurement contracts.
Within-domain comparisons may proceed when unit, denominator, period, geography, method, and attribution align.
Explicit holds identify where activity or reporting structure has not become a comparable outcome.
A direction statement may publish after at least two compatible observations, with a two-point caveat.
Revisions and method breaks can stop, split, or restate a longitudinal series.
A named entity panel may publish after stable identity and at least two compatible observations are verified.
National context and entity performance remain separate layers.
A stable entity panel may deepen into a temporally ordered driver and constraint dossier.
Attribution, independent validation, and alternative explanations can be published without claiming causation.
A later record may narrow, support, challenge, or leave unresolved a named alternative explanation.
Regulator-verified obligations, partial progress, company claims, operator filings, and independent outcomes can remain distinct.
A second cohort can be screened once and then built vertically through the same three evidence layers.
Independent, regulator, operator, company, and carrier-attributed records can remain visibly distinct inside one entity dossier.

what_this_map_does_not_prove: It does not create a cross-portfolio score or ranking.
It does not equate activity, capacity, exposure, service, reliability, safety, cost, or local benefit.
It does not convert company-attributed results into audited causal effects.
It does not turn a two-point movement into a durable trend.
It does not authorize normalization across incompatible domains.
It does not authorize a cross-agency, cross-manufacturer, cross-asset, or cross-carrier ranking.
It does not prove that a named intervention, control, input, commitment, or corrective action caused an observed outcome.
It does not authorize a readiness score, composite score, or entity ranking.
It does not prove that one tested alternative caused the observed outcome.
It does not authorize denominator mixing, causal effects, rankings, composites, or readiness scores.
It does not make the two cohorts or their entities rankable.
It does not convert vertical evidence depth into a causal effect, composite, or readiness score.
That a Closed, Partially Closed, or Open coverage state measures entity performance, readiness, safety, quality, value, or relative standing.
That a current index, governance audit, cumulative total, capacity record, queue entry, or historical extract closes a different operating question.
That a management letter, annual total, cumulative fleet count, recommendation state, ongoing investigation, or constraint event is a complete operating or outcome record.
That first-pass completion, a monthly table, a program commitment, a project plan, or a current catalog check is a complete operating or outcome record.
That evidence acquisition order ranks entities or that a monthly row, constraint entry, event report, intervention plan, or component audit is complete performance.
That a company response is regulator closure, an arrival is formal contractual acceptance, or an audit initiation is an audit result.
That reported current FTEs were caused by an incentive project, a project amount was fully spent, or one intervention is a repeat operating series.
That open recommendation count measures NASA performance, or that either anonymous hospital test represents HHS, CMS, the health sector, or later operations.
That recommendation closure, inventory completeness, portfolio movement, or component remediation measures agency performance, system safety, readiness, quality, value, or causal effect.
That portfolio implementation counts are comparable agency rates or that modeled potential benefits are realized savings.
That FTFN action keys are official GAO recommendation numbers or that a named priority action has been implemented or closed.
That an agency response is implementation, a recommendation status is an entity evidence state, or recommendation closure is an operating outcome.
That a public artifact, agency submission, milestone, or partial addressing constitutes implementation, closure, agency performance, or operating outcome.
